title: Diagnose wear on a Haas SMTC double arm

symptoms: unusual popping or banging sound during a tool change

machine_family.note: Not stated in the narration, title, or TG0128.

subsystem.note: Named in the narration (U0001) and TG0128's title.

task_type.note: Team label: diagnostic inspection. Schema 1.0.0 has no separate 'diagnosis' task type.

steps.title: Check for visual and audible warning signs
Inspect the arm for dings, nicks and gouges on the alignment key and V-flange
Check for end wear indicating incorrect double arm height
Check the locking mechanism if tools are dropping
Position the double arm to check the finger-to-tool-holder clearance
Measure the finger-to-flange gap with a feeler gauge
Adjust the gap with shim washers if it is out of spec
If a servo alarm appears, use it to identify the failed component

locator.text_span: Push down on the plunger and hold it down. Put a tool holder into the arm. During correct operation, the slide moves in. Release the plunger. Try to remove the tool holder. During correct operation, the slide does not move in and the tool holder locks in position. Measure the space between the slide and the tool holder. Use a feeler gauge. The correct space is between 0.014 in (0.36 mm) and 0.020 in (0.51 mm). If the machine is a DM-1 or DT-1, the correct space is between 0.005 in (0.13 mm) and 0.015 in (0.38 mm). Add or remove 0.01 in (0.25 mm) shim washers, part number 45-0075, until the space is correct. Once the gap is set reassemble the slider assembly with the spring and washer installed. Apply a layer of Lithium Tacky Grease to the finger, spring and washer.
